links_touching_record.rationale: This measure is the analytical verification of FB2-SYS-SYR-000003: it sums the waits the pinned source's application configuration applies between the stages of opening and compares the total against the interval the requirement allocates, and it expects the comparison to fail. The link asserts that the timing claim is under verification and under contradicted, not that the requirement is satisfied.

The system requirement refines the stakeholder need FB2-SYS-NED-000003 into a system-level obligation. The need is in stakeholder language and the requirement is measurable; the trace is the derivation step.
The system requirement refines the safety goal FB2-SAF-SGO-000001 at system level, carrying the allocation the safety allocation field on the requirement names.

FB2-SW-SWR-000003 is the lower-level requirement allocated to the system requirement FB2-SYS-SYR-000003. The two statements and acceptance criteria were read against each other before the link was made, so the system requirement is covered indirectly through its allocation rather than directly by a measure of its own.

The system requirement refines the operational scenario's obligation into a measurable system-level statement. The use case is the parent and the requirement is the child, which is the direction refines runs in everywhere in this registry.

The release identification record depends on the safe-state requirement because the end-of-line station's safe-state test is the only check of it that happens after the line, and the release cannot be identified without knowing which reaction it verifies.
The end-of-line plan exercises the safe-state requirement on every item leaving the line, which makes it the requirement's largest-volume verification.
The field monitoring record's safe-state signal is the only production evidence that the safe-state requirement holds in service, which is why that signal is specified with a no-threshold escalation.

record_verbatim.rationale: The system-level statement of the safety goal's objective. It is written at this level because the obligation spans three allocated requirements - the software state machine, the hardware driver path and the hardware feedback path - and a requirement that any one of them could claim to satisfy would let the end-to-end timing go unstated. The figure here is the safety goal's own fault-tolerant time interval; the way that interval is spent is the technical safety concept's business, not this requirement's.

revision_history.author: system_engineer
revision_history.description: System requirement authored because SYS.2 was recorded as a coverage gap with no system requirement record in either profile. System-level: it states what the integrated item must do and allocates to the existing technical requirements rather than restating them.

safety_allocation.mitigation: Latched fault state, auxiliary feedback confirmation, the hardware watchdog path and the independent monitor

standards_mappings.rationale: System requirements analysis: derived from the stakeholder needs and the safety goal, allocated to hardware and software.
Where the requirement carries a safety allocation, this is the level at which it is expressed. Where it does not, the mapping is recorded as not applicable rather than forced.

record_verbatim.statement: On a confirmed safe-operating-area violation the item shall open all high-voltage contactors, disable charging and log the fault within 100 ms of the condition becoming measurable, shall confirm the open state by auxiliary feedback, and shall not leave that state on the fault disappearing.
record_verbatim.title: SYR: the item shall reach and confirm the safe state within the fault-tolerant time interval, and shall latch the condition that required it

shape_note: Deliberately not shaped like a corpus record: no top-level id, profile, artifact_type or source_refs, so that generating packets cannot change any coverage number. See the module docstring of make_review_packets.py.

signature_block._recording: Transcribe a completed signature into the record as human_approval_status plus a revision_history entry naming the reviewer, and archive the signed packet outside docs/artifacts/reviews/packets/.

Filling it in is the only thing that changes human_approval_status on the record, and the corpus rule `human_approval_rejected` fails validation on any record whose human_approval_status is not pending, so no tool can manufacture the state.

signature_policy: The signature block below is empty by construction. This tool has no code path that writes a decision, an approval, a signature or an execution verdict. Filling it is a human action.
